note: A1+ Unit 2 Lesson 2.1, built on 2026-11-19 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. The user approved the A1+ Unit 2 plan on 2026-11-19 (A1+ 2.Y follows A1 2.Y, one grammar step each) and chose "Straight to Preview": no per-lesson gates, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, reviewed in Preview. Each cast member goes to one place: Luis to the gym, Ana to the pool (A1+ 1.3's swimming photo), Diego to the office and Sofia to the park. Learn introduces goes on a known place first (the park), then each new place on its own (It is a gym.) before its contrast pair. Photo banks set the four people and places against each other; Listen text cards set the habit against the I-form and A1's is going. A unit's first lesson keeps Learn models to 8 words and Listen to 2 lines.

lesson.title: 2.1 Where people go
lesson.unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
lesson.unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
lesson.goal: Say where people go with go to and goes to (I go to the gym. / Luis goes to the gym.), with three new places: gym, pool and office.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.1 Places Around Me: A1 names places (It is a park.) and says what people are doing in them (The girl is running in the park.); A1+ 2.1 says where people go. The one new grammar relationship is go to + place with he/she goes, the -es spelling of go, taught against the I-form (I go to the gym. / Luis goes to the gym.) and heard against A1's is going (Luis is going to the gym.). New places: gym, pool, office.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 2.1 places (park) and It is a/an; A1 4.6 go to school; A1 6.3 I am going to; A1 6.11 goes; A1+ 1.2-1.3 the he/she -s; A1+ 1.9 Where does…?; A1+ 1.3 Ana swims and Sofia runs in the park.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say goes with a long o and a final z sound (/ɡoʊz/), different from go; keep to the in go to the gym short. Do not require native-like speed.
